CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole benchmark):
- The binary is /workspace/executable (lz4 v1.10.0 CLI). You may ONLY run it and observe stdout/stderr/exit codes/output files.
- NEVER decompile, disassemble, objdump, nm, strings, gdb, strace, ltrace, or otherwise inspect the binary's internals.
- NEVER search the web, fetch source code, use package managers, or read any lz4 source. Do not install lz4.
- Only interact through the normal CLI interface.
- 'strings' and 'nm' on /workspace/executable are FORBIDDEN.

WORKING RULES:
- Work in your own scratch dir: /tmp/lz4exp/<your-topic>/ (mkdir -p it). Use ABSOLUTE paths everywhere.
- Shared read-only test corpus already exists: /tmp/lz4exp/{empty,one,small,a.txt,zeros64k,rand1m} and /workspace/assets/sample.txt.lz4
- Create your own extra test files as needed inside your scratch dir.
- 'xxd' is NOT installed; use 'od -A d -t x1' or python3 for hex dumps.
- Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY (e.g. cmd >out 2>err; echo $?) and record EXACT text including trailing spaces and newlines. Use 'od -c' when whitespace matters.
- Be exhaustive and systematic. Try edge cases, invalid inputs, weird combinations.
- Write your detailed findings to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/<topic>.md (mkdir -p /tmp/lz4exp/notes). Include verbatim transcripts.


YOUR TOPIC: decompress-basic
Write notes to /tmp/lz4exp/notes/decompress-basic.md

Probe DECOMPRESSION file handling of /workspace/executable.
Cover: 'executable -d x.lz4' default output name; input without .lz4 extension (error text?); -d with explicit output; unlz4-style; decompressing to existing file (prompt / -f); --rm; -c; 'null' output; decompressing a non-lz4 file (error text + exit code); decompressing truncated frame; decompressing corrupted data (flip bytes in header, in block, in checksum, in content checksum); wrong magic; empty input file; input that is only a magic number; concatenated frames (cat a.lz4 b.lz4 > c.lz4); trailing garbage after a frame (1 byte, 3 bytes, 4 bytes of junk); skippable frames (magic 0x184D2A50..0x184D2A5F) alone and interleaved; legacy frame 0x184C2102.
Build inputs with python3. Record exact error text, stream, exit code, and how much output was produced before failure.

When done, RETURN a dense summary (<=120 lines) of the most important, exactly-reproducible facts a reimplementer needs. Include exact message strings in quotes. Do not include filler.

# lz4 v1.10.0 CLI — DECOMPRESSION file handling (topic: decompress-basic)

Binary: `/workspace/executable`. Version banner (stdout, exit 0):
`*** lz4 v1.10.0 64-bit multithread, by Yann Collet ***\n`

All diagnostics go to **stderr**. Payload goes to stdout only with `-c` / `-` / `stdout`
or implicit stdin->stdout.

---

## 1. Output-name derivation

| input | mode | result |
|---|---|---|
| `a.txt.lz4` | `-d a.txt.lz4` | writes `a.txt`, exit 0, input kept |
| `f.tar.lz4` | `-d` | writes `f.tar` |
| `b.lz4.lz4` | `-d` | writes `b.lz4` (strips one suffix) |
| `noext` | `-d noext` | **error**, exit 1 |
| `f.LZ4` | `-d` | **error** (case-sensitive; only lowercase `.lz4`) |
| `f.lz` | `-d` | **error** |
| `.lz4` | `-d` | **error** (stripped name would be empty) |

Error text (stderr), exit 1 — the "Cannot determine..." line is followed by
`Incorrect parameters\n` and the SHORT usage block:

```
Cannot determine an output filename \nIncorrect parameters\nUsage : \n      executable [arg] [input] [output] \n\ninput   : a filename \n          with no FILE, or when FILE is - or stdin, read standard input\nArguments : \n -1     : fast compression (default) \n -12    : slowest compression level \n -T#    : use # threads for compression (default:0==auto) \n -d     : decompression (default for .lz4 extension)\n -f     : overwrite output without prompting \n -k     : preserve source files(s)  (default) \n--rm    : remove source file(s) after successful de/compression \n -h/-H  : display help/long help and exit \n
```

`.lz4` extension implies decompression even without `-d`:
`executable a.txt.lz4` == `executable -d a.txt.lz4`.

## 2. Normal success output (stderr)

Auto-derived output name, default verbosity:
```
b'Decoding file a.txt \n\rDecompressed : 0 MiB  \r<79 spaces>\ra.txt.lz4                      : decoded 135 bytes \n'
```
Components:
- `"Decoding file %s \n"` — %s is the **derived output** name. **Only printed when the
  output name was auto-derived.** Absent when output given explicitly / stdout / null / -t / -m.
- progress refresh `"\rDecompressed : %llu MiB  "` (MiB truncated down) — **timing dependent,
  may or may not appear**; verified nondeterministic across identical runs.
- clear sequence = `"\r"` + 79 spaces + `"\r"`.
- summary `"%-30.30s : decoded %llu bytes \n"` with the **input** filename, **truncated to 30 chars**
  (e.g. `/tmp/lz4exp/decompress-basic/w` for a longer path).

Verbosity: `-q` removes "Decoding file", progress, and summary (errors kept).
`-qq` removes errors too (exit code unchanged). `-v` prepends the version banner and appends
`Done in 0.00 s ==> 0.14 MiB/s  (cpu load : 107%)\n`. `-vv` adds
`_POSIX_C_SOURCE defined: 200809L\n_POSIX_VERSION defined: 200809L\nPLATFORM_POSIX_VERSION defined: 200809L\n`.

## 3. Explicit output / stdout / null

- `-d in out` → writes `out`, **no "Decoding file" line**.
- `-c`, output `-`, output `stdout` → payload to stdout, **stderr completely silent**.
- output `null` → decodes, discards, prints normal summary; no file named `null` created.
- `-t` / `--test` → same as `null`: summary printed, exit 0; on bad input exit = decode error code.
- stdin (no file arg, or `-`, or `stdin`) → implicitly writes to stdout, silent. Empty stdin → exit 0, no output, no message.
- 3 positional args: `Error : out2 won't be used ! Do you want multiple input files (-m) ? \n`, exit 1.

## 4. unlz4 / lz4cat (argv[0] dispatch)

- Match is a **substring** test: `unlz4`, `unlz4-xyz`, `myunlz4` all force `-d`.
- `lz4cat` = `-d -c` + quiet (no stderr on success).
- **`lz4cat` on an unrecognized (non-lz4) file copies it verbatim to stdout, exit 0** (pass-through).
  Pass-through applies only when the *first* magic is unrecognized; a valid frame followed by
  garbage still errors (34), and a valid magic with a bad header still errors (34).
  `executable -d -c -m bin.dat` (non-lz4) → `Error 44`, i.e. pass-through is lz4cat-only.

## 5. Existing output file / -f / --rm / -k

Prompt when destination exists and `-f` absent (stderr):
```
a.txt already exists; do you want to overwrite (y/N) ? 
```
- refusal (EOF, `n`, anything not y/Y) appends `    not overwritten  \n` (4 spaces before, 2 before \n) → **exit 1**, dest untouched.
- `y`, `Y`, `yes` → proceeds, exit 0.
- `-f` skips the prompt entirely.

`--rm`: deletes the source after a **successful** decode. Not deleted on failure.
**`--rm -c` still deletes the source** even though output went to stdout.
`-k` and `--rm` are **last-one-wins** (`--rm -k` keeps, `-k --rm` removes).

## 6. File-open ordering (important)

The **destination is opened/truncated BEFORE the source is opened**:
- `-d nosuch.lz4` leaves a 0-byte file `nosuch` on disk and prints
  `Decoding file nosuch \nnosuch.lz4: No such file or directory \n` (exit 1).
- `-d -f self.lz4 self.lz4` **destroys the input**: prints `self.lz4 : decoded 0 bytes \n`, exit 0,
  file left at 0 bytes.
- Every decode error below also leaves a (possibly 0-byte / partial) destination file behind.

Other file errors:
- input is a directory: `lz4: adir.lz4 is a directory -- ignored \n`, exit 1.
- output is a directory: `dd: Is a directory\n` (no trailing space), exit 1.

## 7. Error codes and exact messages

All of form `Error %d : <text> \n` (note the space before `\n`).

| code | message | trigger |
|---|---|---|
| 26 | `LZ4F frame decoding could not complete: invalid frame ` | truncated frame / missing endmark / missing content-checksum / 1..6 trailing garbage bytes / truncated skippable **after** an LZ4F frame |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_headerVersion_wrong ` | FLG version bits != 01 |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_reservedFlag_set ` | FLG bit1 set, or BD bit7 set |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_maxBlockSize_invalid ` | BD value <4 (e.g. 0x00,0x30); also a block whose size exceeds the declared max |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_headerChecksum_invalid ` | HC byte wrong (incl. BD=0x70 with stale HC) |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_blockChecksum_invalid ` | block data or block checksum corrupted (frames with BX) |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_contentChecksum_invalid ` | trailing xxh32 corrupted |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_frameSize_wrong ` | `--content-size` value != actual (declared 0 is accepted/ignored) |
| 34 | `Decompression error : ERROR_frameType_unknown ` | >=7 bytes of trailing garbage after an LZ4F frame; **legacy frame appended after an LZ4F frame** |
| 40 | `Unrecognized header : Magic Number unreadable ` | input shorter than 4 bytes (1..3) |
| 42 | `Stream error : skippable size unreadable ` | skippable magic at stream start with <4 bytes of size field |
| 43 | `Stream error : cannot skip skippable area ` | skippable size overruns EOF **on a pipe** (seekable file: silently accepted, exit 0) |
| 44 | `Unrecognized header : file cannot be decoded ` | >=4 bytes, unknown magic (plain text, 0x184D2A4F, 0x184D2A60, ...) |
| 61 | `Error: cannot read block size in Legacy format ` | 1..3 trailing bytes after a legacy frame (message is literally `Error 61 : Error: ...`) |
| 63 | `Read error : cannot access compressed block ! ` | truncated legacy block |
| 64 | `Decoding Failed ! Corrupted input detected ! ` | legacy block with size 0 |

Warning (not `Error`), **exit 1**, output kept and summary still printed:
`Stream followed by undecodable data at position %llu \n` — legacy path, >=4 trailing
bytes that are not a recognized magic. Position = offset after consuming those 4 bytes.

## 8. Partial output on failure

- LZ4F, stored (uncompressed) blocks, truncated mid-block: bytes decoded so far ARE written
  (154-byte frame cut to 100 → 89-byte output) then exit 26.
- LZ4F, compressed blocks, truncated: nothing written (0 bytes), all-or-nothing per block.
- Trailing-garbage errors after a complete frame: the full valid payload IS written, then error.
- Legacy error 61: output is written up to the last flushed buffer boundary and the tail is
  **lost** (21 MB legacy stream + 1 junk byte → only 3 276 800 bytes written, a true prefix).

## 9. Frame concatenation / trailing data

- `cat a.lz4 b.lz4 > c.lz4` → concatenated payloads, exit 0. Works for N frames, and with
  zero-length frames on either side.
- Trailing garbage after an LZ4F frame: 1–6 bytes → exit 26; >=7 bytes → exit 34
  `ERROR_frameType_unknown`. 4 bytes of `04 22 4d 18` (bare magic) → exit 26.
- Empty input file (0 bytes) → **exit 0**, 0-byte output, no message.
- Only the 4-byte magic `04 22 4d 18` → exit 26.
- Magic twice (`04 22 4d 18 04 22 4d 18`) → exit 34 `ERROR_headerVersion_wrong`.
- Empty legacy magic only (`02 21 4c 18`) → exit 0, 0-byte output.

## 10. Skippable frames (magic 0x184D2A50..0x184D2A5F)

- All 16 magics accepted; 0x184D2A4F and 0x184D2A60 → exit 44.
- Alone → exit 0, empty output. Before a frame, after a frame, and between two frames all work.
- Handled by two different code paths:
  - **at stream start**: CLI's own skipper. On a **seekable file** an oversized/overrunning
    size field is silently tolerated (`fseek` past EOF) → exit 0. On a **pipe** → exit 43.
    A missing/short size field → exit 42.
  - **after an LZ4F frame**: handled inside LZ4F; any truncation or oversized size → exit 26
    on both files and pipes (never 42/43).

## 11. Legacy frames (magic 0x184C2102)

- Produced by `-l`; decoded transparently, exit 0, no special message.
- `legacy + legacy`, `legacy + LZ4F`, `legacy + skippable`, `legacy + skippable + legacy` all work.
- **`LZ4F + legacy` FAILS** with exit 34 `ERROR_frameType_unknown` (asymmetric: the LZ4F path
  never hands control back to the outer magic dispatcher, but the legacy path does).
- Legacy block size 0 → exit 64. Truncated legacy block → exit 63. Absurd block size
  (0x7fffffff) → treated as "not a block": warning at §7, exit 1, 0 bytes output.

## 12. Frame-header semantics verified

- FLG version bits must be `01`; FLG bit1 (reserved) must be 0; DictID bit accepted (ID ignored
  when no `-D`); BD must be 4..7 (0x40/0x50/0x60/0x70); BD bit7 reserved must be 0.
- `--content-size` value is verified; **a declared size of 0 is accepted regardless of actual size**.
- Header checksum = `(XXH32(FLG..end-of-optional-fields, seed=0) >> 8) & 0xFF` (verified: for
  `64 40` HC = 0xa7).
- Minimal empty frame produced by the tool: `04 22 4d 18 64 40 a7 00 00 00 00 05 5d cc 02` (15 B).

## 13. `-m` (multiple files)

- `-m` implies auto output names and is **silent at default verbosity** (no per-file summary).
  `-m -v` prints per-file summary lines plus the `Done in ... MiB/s` line.
- **Aborts at the first failing file** (later files not processed); exit = that file's error code.
- `-m -c` concatenates all payloads to stdout.

## 14. Misc

- `-d` and `-z` are last-one-wins (`-d -z` compresses, `-z -d` decompresses).
- `--` works as an end-of-options separator.
- Sparse output is ON by default when writing to a file: 1 MiB of zeros decompresses to an
  apparent 1048576-byte file occupying 8 disk blocks; `--no-sparse` gives 2048 blocks.

## Partial output before failure
Stored (uncompressed) LZ4F block truncated → decoded prefix IS written (154 B frame cut to 100 → 89 B out) then exit 26. Compressed blocks truncated → 0 bytes (all-or-nothing per block). Trailing-garbage errors → full valid payload written first. Legacy error 61 → prefix written but tail **lost** (21 MB + 1 junk byte → exactly 3 276 800 B, verified true prefix). A dest file is always left behind, even 0-byte.

## Concatenation / trailing data
`cat a.lz4 b.lz4` concatenates payloads, exit 0 (N frames, empty frames anywhere). Trailing junk: 1–6 B → 26; ≥7 B → 34. Empty 0-byte input → **exit 0**, empty output, no message. Bare `04 22 4d 18` → 26. Bare `02 21 4c 18` → exit 0, empty.

## Skippable (0x184D2A50–0x184D2A5F)
All 16 accepted; ±1 outside range → 44. Alone / before / after / between frames all exit 0. Two distinct code paths: **at stream start** the CLI skips via fseek — an overrunning size is silently tolerated on a seekable file (exit 0) but gives 43 on a pipe, and a short size field gives 42. **After an LZ4F frame** LZ4F handles it internally — any truncation/overrun gives 26 on both files and pipes.

## Legacy (0x184C2102)
Decoded transparently, exit 0, no special message. `legacy+legacy`, `legacy+LZ4F`, `legacy+skippable`, `legacy+skip+legacy` all work. **`LZ4F+legacy` fails with 34 `ERROR_frameType_unknown`** — asymmetric: the legacy decoder returns to the outer magic dispatcher, the LZ4F decoder never does.

## Header semantics verified
Version bits must be `01`; FLG bit1 reserved must be 0; DictID bit accepted (ID ignored without `-D`); BD ∈ {0x40,0x50,0x60,0x70}; BD bit7 must be 0. HC = `(XXH32(FLG..optional, seed 0) >> 8) & 0xFF` (for `64 40` → `0xa7`). Minimal empty frame: `04 22 4d 18 64 40 a7 00 00 00 00 05 5d cc 02`.

## -m and misc
`-m` implies auto names, is **silent at default verbosity**, and **aborts at the first failing file** (later inputs untouched; exit = that error code). `-m -v` prints per-file summaries + `Done in ...`. `-m -c` concatenates to stdout. `-d`/`-z` last-one-wins. `--` works as separator. Sparse output is on by default for files (1 MiB of zeros → 8 disk blocks; `--no-sparse` → 2048).
